summary:
We developed ASTRO-MED HRP, a 100% autonomous, offline-first clinical console that combines the "Astro" voice assistant with the 3N Harness (Arnés 3N) to protect astronaut health during deep-space exploration missions. Inspired by the Canadian Space Agency's (CSA) Bio-Monitor architecture, the harness continuously measures 13 vital signs through a textile thoracic vest, a forehead headband, a dosimeter wristband, and a laryngeal collar.

Beyond continuous monitoring, the system evaluates NASA-STD-3001 standards and calculates radiation exposure in millisieverts based on the mission environment (ISS, Cislunar Transit, Moon, or Mars). When it detects an anomaly, it automatically shifts the visual alert level and guides the crew with step-by-step medical recommendations, solving communication delays of up to 20 minutes with Earth.
details:
ASTRO-MED HRP: Autonomous Clinical Console and 3-Node Wearable Telemetry System for Deep-Space Exploration

1. System Functionality and Operational Architecture

ASTRO-MED HRP (astro-health-monitor) is a 100% autonomous, offline-first aerospace clinical console engineered for continuous physiological monitoring, preventive diagnostics, and medical triage of astronauts during deep-space exploration missions (National Aeronautics and Space Administration [NASA] Human Research Program [HRP], 2023). The system integrates three operational layers: the 3N Wearable Harness (Arnés 3N), an environmental physics adaptation engine, and an interactive clinical console assisted by the "Astro" offline voice synthesizer.

Wearable Hardware Architecture: The 3N Harness (13 Continuous Vital Signs 24/7)

Grounded in the flight-validated Bio-Monitor / Astroskin system developed by the Canadian Space Agency (CSA, 2019) and tested aboard the International Space Station (ISS) during Expeditions 58 and 59 (NASA Life Sciences Data Archive [LSDA] & CSA, 2020), our physical hardware prototype centers on a modular 3-node body area network. This garment passively captures 13 continuous physiological parameters without skin-irritating adhesive gels or cumbersome cables:

  • Node 1. Smart Thoracic Vest (7 Continuous Parameters).

    1. Heart Rate (bpm): Captured via silver-coated textile electrodes at 256 Hz, operating within a nominal clinical range of 50–100 bpm and triggering alerts at < 45 bpm or > 110 bpm (NASA, 2023).
    2. Heart Rate Variability (hrvRmssdMs): Real-time calculation of the root mean square of successive RR interval differences at 256 Hz (nominal > 20 ms; alert triggered upon a > 30% drop from individual baseline) to quantify autonomic fatigue and physiological stress (NASA LSDA & CSA, 2020).
    3. 3-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG): Continuous QRS waveform morphology tracking at 256 Hz for early detection of microgravity-induced arrhythmias or ectopic beats (CSA, 2019; NASA, 2023).
    4. Respiratory Rate (respiratoryRateRpm): Measured via dual thoracic and abdominal Respiratory Inductance Plethysmography (RIP) bands at 128 Hz, with a nominal range of 12–20 rpm and clinical alerts at < 10 rpm or > 24 rpm (NASA, 2023; NASA LSDA & CSA, 2020).
    5. Minute Ventilation (minuteVentilationLpm): Volumetric estimation of air moved per minute derived from RIP thoracoabdominal expansion at 128 Hz (nominal 5.0–8.0 L/min; alert on a > 40% resting increase indicating potential cabin hypercapnia; NASA, 2026).
    6. Peripheral Skin Temperature (skinTempC): Lateral textile thermistor sampled at 1 Hz (nominal 32.0–35.5 °C) to evaluate peripheral thermoregulation and circadian thermal rhythm (NASA LSDA & CSA, 2020).
    7. Physical Activity, Posture, and Sleep Efficiency (postureScore, sleepHours): Triaxial MEMS accelerometer sampled at 64 Hz to quantify biomechanical load, posture, and sleep architecture against a target of 6.5–8.0 h per 24-hour cycle (CSA, 2019; NASA, 2023).
  • Node 2. Forehead Headband (4 Continuous Parameters). Strategically positioned over the supraorbital artery on the forehead to compensate for microgravity cephalad fluid shift—wherein 1.5 to 2.0 L of blood and interstitial fluid migrate from the lower extremities toward the thorax and head, providing a significantly more stable optical signal than the wrist (CSA, 2019; Platts et al., 2016): 8. Continuous Cuffless Blood Pressure (systolicBP, diastolicBP): Estimated beat-to-beat (nominal 90–120 / 60–80 mmHg) by calculating Pulse Transit Time (pttMs, nominal 150–250 ms) between the thoracic ECG R-wave peak and the arrival of the forehead photoplethysmographic pulse wave (CSA, 2019; Hughson et al., 2016). 9. Arterial Oxygen Saturation (SpO₂, spo2Percent): Dual-wavelength red and infrared reflective photoplethysmography (PPG) at 64 Hz (nominal 95–100%; caution < 92%; critical < 88%; NASA, 2023). 10. Tissue Perfusion Index (perfusionIndex): Ratio of pulsatile to non-pulsatile forehead blood flow at 64 Hz (nominal 1.0–10.0%; early peripheral vasoconstriction alert < 0.5%; NASA HRP, 2023). 11. Core Body Temperature (bodyTempC): Forehead Zero-Heat-Flux thermal sensor at 1 Hz that thermally isolates deep core temperature from ambient cabin air (nominal 36.5–37.5 °C; critical > 38.0 °C or < 35.5 °C; NASA, 2023).
  • Node 3. Dosimeter Wristband and Laryngeal Collar (2 Continuous Parameters). 12. Daily Rate and Cumulative Ionizing Radiation Dose (dailyRadiationMsv, cumulativeRadiationMsv): Active electronic micro-dosimeter (Radi-N2 / MOSFET) sampling every 1 min in millisieverts (mSv), enforcing operational thresholds of 0.65 mSv/d (nominal), 1.45 mSv/d (caution), 200 mSv (annual limit), and 600 mSv (NASA career limit) / 1,000 mSv (CSA career limit; CSA, 2022; NASA, 2023). 13. Vocal Acoustic Biomarkers: Piezoelectric laryngeal contact sensor measuring vocal cord micro-vibrations to detect physical fatigue and neuromuscular tension with complete immunity to ambient Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) fan noise (NASA HRP, 2021, 2023).

Mathematical Clinical Engine (healthEngine.ts), Hemodynamic Indices, and Four Mission Environments

From the 13 continuous streams of the 3N Harness, the mathematical engine computes three real-time derived hemodynamic indices to anticipate circulatory collapse before systolic blood pressure declines (NASA, 2023; Platts et al., 2016):

  • Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP): Calculated as MAP = DBP + (SBP − DBP) / 3 (nominal 70–100 mmHg; critical < 65 mmHg, indicating vital organ hypoperfusion).
  • Pulse Pressure (PP): Calculated as PP = SBP − DBP (nominal 30–50 mmHg; alert < 25 mmHg, reflecting reduced stroke volume).
  • Shock Index (SI): Calculated as SI = HR / SBP (nominal 0.50–0.70; critical ≥ 0.90, alerting to occult hypovolemia or imminent orthostatic shock).
  • Deterministic Global Readiness Formula: Calculated as Global Readiness = round(Mean of 6 Anatomical Zones × 0.75 + Circadian Routine Stability × 0.25) (Basner et al., 2022; NASA, 2023).

Furthermore, the console models the astrophysical and habitability conditions of four mission environments (missionData.ts) in accordance with NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 and Volume 2 (NASA, 2023, 2026):

  1. International Space Station (iss, Low Earth Orbit, 408 km): Gravity 0.00 g; radiation 0.45 mSv/d (partial magnetospheric shielding); one-way communication latency 0.4 s (TDRS network); cabin atmosphere 101.3 kPa and 2.3 mmHg CO₂.
  2. Cislunar / Deep-Space Transit (nave): Gravity 0.00 g; radiation 1.25 mSv/d (direct Galactic Cosmic Ray exposure); latency 110 s (Deep Space Network); cabin atmosphere 70.3 kPa and 3.1 mmHg CO₂.
  3. Lunar Surface (luna, Artemis South Pole Base): Gravity 0.16 g; radiation 0.95 mSv/d; latency 2.6 s (Lunar Gateway Ka-Band); cabin atmosphere 56.5 kPa and 2.8 mmHg CO₂.
  4. Martian Surface (marte, Rover Sol 142): Gravity 0.38 g; radiation 1.65 mSv/d; latency 860 s (14 min 20 s one-way); cabin atmosphere 58.0 kPa and 3.4 mmHg CO₂.

30-Second Oscillometric Recalibration Protocol. The software mandates calibrating cuffless PTT against a brachial oscillometric cuff every 24 h to correct drift caused by the 17–30% increase in carotid artery stiffness documented during long-duration spaceflight in the BP Reg experiment (Hughson et al., 2016). Additionally, recalibration is triggered automatically upon transitioning from microgravity (0.00 g) to partial gravity (0.16 g on the Moon or 0.38 g on Mars) to prevent orthostatic intolerance syncope prior to Extravehicular Activities (EVA; Platts et al., 2016).

Autonomous Clinical Console, Automatic Hazard Detection, and "Astro" Voice Assistant

  • Automatic Hazard Level Detection (Zero Manual Panic Button): The persistent top mission bar (TopMissionBar.tsx) continuously evaluates clinical thresholds and dynamically shifts its chromatic state without requiring manual crew activation (NASA HRP, 2023). In Nominal state, it remains unobtrusive; in Caution, it triggers a preventive amber alert; and in Critical Hazard, it shifts to high-priority red, recommending immediate physician contact when latency is < 60 s (ISS or Moon) or providing one-click navigation to autonomous clinical protocols when Earth communication is unavailable (Transit, Mars, or offline mode).
    1. Monitor (OverviewBentoGrid.tsx): Displays a 6-body-system integrity donut chart, environmental physics card, biometric summary modules, vital trend curve, and an Offline Local Clinical Logbook.
    2. Anatomical Scanner (AnatomicalScanner.tsx): Interactive vector human silhouette divided into six anatomical systems: Brain and Central Nervous System (Basner et al., 2015), Face and Neuro-Ocular System for Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS; Mader et al., 2022), Heart and Cardiovascular System (Hughson et al., 2016; Platts et al., 2016), Endocrine and Metabolic System (Garrett-Bakelman et al., 2019), Abdomen and Renal Function, and Musculoskeletal System (Sibonga et al., 2017). Each zone provides three tabs: (a) Examination & Action Protocol, (b) Alert & Triage Thresholds (NASA-STD-3001), and (c) Clinical Rationale & 5 NASA HRP Hazards.
    3. 3N Harness (WearableHarnessPanel.tsx): Real-time node telemetry, sampling frequencies in Hz, derived hemodynamic indices, and the 30-second oscillometric calibration workflow (CSA, 2019).
    4. Biomarkers (BiomarkersDashboard.tsx): Organized into Physical Signs (8) (cortisol, circadian melatonin, blood glucose/insulin resistance, hydration/plasma volume, bone mineral density, physical fatigue; CSA, 2020; Garrett-Bakelman et al., 2019; Sibonga et al., 2017), Streamlined BHP Mental Health (4 core indicators)—Stress Level, Psychomotor Vigilance Reaction Time PVT (< 280 ms; Basner et al., 2015), Facial Tension, and Stimulation/Sleep (NASA HRP, 2021)—and the Circadian Routine Detector tracking sleep schedule deviation, 2.5 L water intake, meals, and 120 min Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) sessions (NASA, 2023).
    5. Habits (TelemetryCharts.tsx, RecommendedHabitsPanel.tsx, HabitsExplanationPanel.tsx): Historical telemetry charts paired with an interactive NASA-STD-3001 preventive countermeasure checklist and clinical rationale (NASA, 2023).
    6. Science (ScientificFrameworkSection.tsx, ScientificReferencesContent.tsx): Technical matrix of the five NASA HRP hazards, CSA operational dosimetry limits (CSA, 2022), and an auditable library of 16 verified scientific references.
    7. Capture / Manual Modal (MultimodalScanModal.tsx): When the 3N Harness detects an anomaly, the software guides the crew to perform on-demand assessments using standard cabin equipment: AI Camera (optical facial tension and posture analysis via live webcam or 2D simulator) and Clinical Manual Entry for Point-of-Care biochemical parameters (CSA, 2020; NASA HRP, 2023).

2. System Benefits

  • Complete Medical Autonomy (100% Offline-First): Eliminates reliance on cloud servers, internet connectivity, or real-time links with Mission Control, enabling millisecond diagnostics and triage during communication blackouts or 20-minute one-way Mars delays (NASA HRP, 2023).
  • Non-Invasive 24/7 Ergonomics: Replaces hospital cabling, skin-irritating adhesive gel electrodes, and repetitive pneumatic cuffs with a breathable smart garment that never impedes daily tasks or EVA suit operations (CSA, 2019; NASA LSDA & CSA, 2020).
  • Zero Cognitive Overload During Emergencies: By replacing manual panic buttons and lengthy subjective questionnaires with automatic hazard detection and hands-free audio guidance from "Astro", any crew member can execute critical triage protocols in seconds (Basner et al., 2022; NASA HRP, 2023).
  • Predictive and Preventive Medicine: Cross-references daily countermeasure adherence (sleep, hydration, and ARED exercise) with early hemodynamic markers (Shock Index and HRV drops) to correct physiological drift before acute clinical failure occurs (NASA, 2023; Platts et al., 2016).

3. Intended Project Impact

  • Deep-Space Exploration (Moon to Mars): Delivers a deployable hardware-software architecture ready to support Artemis lunar surface operations, the Lunar Gateway, and human missions to Mars, directly fulfilling NASA Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC) autonomous medical operations requirements (NASA HRP, 2023).
  • Terrestrial Healthcare Transfer: Combining a multiparameter wearable harness with a static clinical console that operates 100% offline resolves a pressing public health challenge on Earth: bringing ICU-grade guided diagnostics and triage to isolated rural clinics without specialist physicians, natural disaster zones with collapsed telecommunications, submarines, Antarctic stations, and high-altitude rescue expeditions (CSA, 2019; NASA HRP, 2023).

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software

  • Core Languages and Frameworks: TypeScript, React 19, Next.js 16.4.6 (App Router configured with static export output: "export" for 100% serverless local execution), HTML5, and Tailwind CSS v4.
  • Scientific Visualization, Audio, and Computer Vision: Recharts for telemetry time-series; deterministic mathematical SVG generators for real-time physiological waveforms (QRS complex, dicrotic PPG wave, and RIP respiratory cycle) and interactive anatomical scanning; Lucide Icons; Web Speech API (window.speechSynthesis) for the offline "Astro" voice assistant; and MediaDevices WebRTC / HTML5 Canvas 2D API (getUserMedia and getImageData luminance matrix analysis) for the AI Camera module.
  • Persistence and Infrastructure: Persistent local storage via localStorage ("astro-med-hrp-state-v1") with backward-compatible state hydration, Git and GitHub version control (oluvalero-ui/astro-health-monitor), and production deployment on Firebase Hosting (https://astro-health-monitor.web.app).
  • Reference Hardware Architecture: Sensor specification grounded in the CSA Bio-Monitor / Astroskin silver-textile ECG and RIP bands (CSA, 2019; NASA LSDA & CSA, 2020), dual-wavelength forehead PPG, Zero-Heat-Flux core thermometry (NASA, 2023), Point-of-Care capillary/salivary assay workflows (CSA, 2020), and Radi-N2 MOSFET electronic dosimetry (CSA, 2022).

5. Project Creativity and Innovation

  • Coupling Environmental Astrophysics with Human Physiology: Unlike conventional medical dashboards that evaluate vital signs in isolation, ASTRO-MED HRP mathematically links destination astrophysics—gravity (g), ionizing radiation (mSv/d), barometric pressure (kPa), cabin CO₂ (mmHg), and communication latency (s)—with the astronaut's real-time hemodynamic and neurocognitive response (CSA, 2022; NASA, 2023, 2026).
  • Aerospace Cockpit Interface (Crew Dragon / ICU) with 100% Semantic Color: We engineered a high-contrast dark interface (#070c17) free of decorative visual noise, where every chromatic shift conveys strict clinical meaning (cyan/emerald = nominal, amber = caution, red = critical hazard; NASA, 2026).
  • Proactive Autonomous Triage and Hands-Free Voice ("Astro"): Rather than waiting for a dizzy or hypoxic astronaut to locate an emergency button, the console automatically detects hazard severity, transforms the top status bar, and vocalizes rescue steps through the "Astro" voice assistant (NASA HRP, 2023).

6. Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Official Regulatory Rigor (NASA and CSA): All clinical and habitability thresholds were audited against NASA-STD-3001_VOL_1 (Revision C, Crew Health) (NASA, 2023), NASA-STD-3001_VOL_2 (Revision F, Habitability and Environmental Health) (NASA, 2026), the NASA HRP Evidence Reports across all five spaceflight hazards (NASA HRP, 2021, 2023), and the CSA Radiation Protection Guidelines (CSA, 2022).
    1. Cephalad fluid shift to justify why PPG and PTT must be measured on a forehead headband rather than a wrist wearable (CSA, 2019; Platts et al., 2016).
    2. The 17–30% increase in carotid artery stiffness and inflight insulin resistance (BP Reg experiment; Hughson et al., 2016) alongside 10–15% plasma volume loss (Platts et al., 2016) to mandate oscillometric cuff recalibration upon landing on the Moon or Mars.
    3. Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) (Mader et al., 2022), spaceflight-induced bone demineralization of 1.0–1.5% per month (Sibonga et al., 2017), multidimensional genomic/endocrine shifts (Garrett-Bakelman et al., 2019), and closed-cabin hypercapnia risks (NASA, 2026).
  • Hardware Realism and Cognitive Friction Reduction: In alignment with official evaluation criteria (NASA Space Apps Challenge, 2026), we focused our physical hardware scope exclusively on the 3N Harness (13 continuous vital signs)—leveraging proven ISS flight heritage (CSA, 2019)—while handling secondary assessments via software using standard cabin tablets and cameras. Finally, we pruned lengthy subjective psychological surveys and redundant manual controls to guarantee a fast, uncluttered interface built to save lives in seconds (Basner et al., 2015, 2022).
